questions.q: What four things does `aws configure` prompt for, in order?
options: Access key ID, secret access key, default region name, default output format
Username, password, default region, and billing account
IAM role ARN, MFA code, region, and VPC ID
Root account email, password, region, and output format
questions.explain: aws configure asks for exactly those four values and writes them to two local files.

questions.q: Which file does `aws configure` use to store the access key ID and secret access key?
options: ~/.aws/credentials
~/.aws/config
~/.ssh/known_hosts
A hidden database managed entirely by the AWS console
questions.explain: ~/.aws/credentials holds the secret material; ~/.aws/config holds region and output format.

questions.q: Which file stores the default region and default output format set by `aws configure`?
options: ~/.aws/config
~/.aws/credentials
~/.aws/profile
They are stored only in environment variables, never on disk
questions.explain: ~/.aws/config holds settings like region and output; credentials is reserved for the access keys.

questions.q: A named profile called `prod` is created with `aws configure --profile prod`. How is its section named in ~/.aws/config compared to ~/.aws/credentials?
options: [profile prod] in ~/.aws/config, but just [prod] in ~/.aws/credentials
[prod] in both files, with no difference
[profile prod] in both files
Named profiles are never written to either file
questions.explain: Every profile section in ~/.aws/config except default gets a literal "profile" prefix; credentials sections never do.

questions.q: What does adding `--profile prod` to a command like `aws s3 ls --profile prod` do?
options: Runs the command using the credentials and settings stored under the "prod" profile instead of default
Changes the command to run against AWS's production API endpoint only
Has no effect unless combined with --region
Deletes the default profile and replaces it with prod
questions.explain: --profile selects which independent set of credentials/settings the CLI uses for that call.
